answers: Yes, barbecuing is allowed in some New York State Parks, but rules vary by park. It is best to check ahead with the specific park you plan to visit to see if barbecuing is permitted. Charcoal grills are typically available at Lighthouse Park and by the West Seawall near the Octagon building on Roosevelt Island, but personal or portable grills are prohibited. Always dispose of used charcoal remnants responsibly.

history.content: I am planning to go camping this summer. What are the places in New York State to do?

There are many ways to experience New York’s great outdoors you can go camping in various state parks across New York. It has more than 5 million acres, 7,000 lakes and streams, and 52,000 miles of rivers and streams for you to explore.  Some notable camping locations include the Adirondack and Catskill Parks, where you can find campsites near the St. Lawrence River, beautiful lakes, the "Grand Canyon of the East," and the woods. For reservations and more information, you can visit their website or call 1-800-456-CAMP. Additionally, the NYSDEC provides information on camping, including primitive camping, in different regions of New York State. Y
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask.
Yes, I do. Are those places free or do I need to pay a fee to park my car and my tent?

Yes, there is a fee to park your car and set up a tent in most New York State Parks. The fees vary depending on the location and amenities offered. For example, electric and full hook-up campsites, waterfront/oceanfront, tent platform, and weekend/holiday use may have additional fees. Out-of-state residents will pay an extra $5/night for campsites and an extra $7/night for cabins/cottages and yurts. Most New York State Parks charge a vehicle use fee between $6 and $10 dollars for day use. You  can also buy the easy-to-use Empire Pass card for $80 and your key to all-season enjoyment with unlimited day-use entry at most facilities operated by State Parks and the State Dept.
I need to take my dog with me . Is it permitted to take dogs on the New York `s campgrounds?

Yes, dogs are allowed in most New York campgrounds, but they must be on a leash no longer than 6ft and under control at all times. However, there are some restrictions on where dogs are allowed within the campgrounds. For example, dogs are not permitted in buildings, undeveloped areas, or on trails, unless specifically designated as being open to dogs on leash. Also, dogs are not allowed on most beaches. It's always a good idea to check the specific rules for the park you plan to visit before you go.  Dogs also can not be left unattended in vehicles or other areas of the park. Proof of appropriate immunizations and valid licenses may be required for any animal brought onto state park property.
I am so glad I can take my dog!
I'm glad you're happy about that! Do you have another question!
I never went to camping before. Do I need to have any vaccines?
I  do not have specific information on whether you need any vaccines to camping in New York State Parks,
